FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Conductors and Accessories for Overhead Lines Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. This Indian Standard has been prepared to lay down the technical requirements Copper Conductors' for use in jumper wires. of `Annealed Stranded

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

ANNEALED STRANDED COPPER CONDUCTORS FOR JUMPER WIRES SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE tl This specikation Covers the requirements for bare stranded annealed copper conductors of concentrio and rope lay ( having concentric stranded members) construction for use as jumper wires in 25 kV ac at 50 Hz single phase traction overhead equipment. 2 REPERENCES

33 Direction of Lay The direction of lay is defined as right hand or left hand. With right hand lay,;the wires conform to the direction of the central part of the letter Z, when the conductor is held vertically. With left hand lay, the wires conform to the direction of the central part of the letter,S, when the conductor is held vertically.

5.2 Condition of the Conductor The conductor shall be supplied plain, without tinning or any other coating in the lengths specified by the purchaser. 5.3 Lay The direction of lay of the outer layer shall be right handed. Successive layers' shall have opposite directions of lay.
5.4 19/1.80 mm Conductor - Concentric Lay The lay length shall neither be less than 10.times

7 TESTS

7.1 All the tests specified in the specification shall be carried out by wires at the manufacturer works. The manufacturer shall arrange all the necessary machinery, apparatus, labour assistance required for conducting the tests without taking any claim on the purchaser. The tests for which the facilities are not available at the manufacturers works may be carried out at any other reputed laboratory with the prior approval of the purchaser. 7.2 TypeTests The following shall constitute type tests :

8.2.1.2 The wires and conductor in the rejected drum shall be cut into lengths of less than 5 m to prevent their inadvertent mwng with other drums. 9 TESTING METHODS 9.1 Visual Examination When examined visually, the wires and conductors shall be smooth, free from harmful defects such as abrasions, peelings, rough surface and bird caging. 9.2 Measurement of Diameter of Wires and Stranded Conductor The diameter shall be measured by means of ratchet micrometer or a dial micrometer between two flat circular studs of minimum diameter of 5 mm. The measurements shall be taken at 5 places of the sample. The average dia of the strands shall be within the limits prescribed in 4.5.
9.3 Lay Lengths The lay lengths shall be measured for the complete conductor. The lay length of different layers shall be within the limits prescribed in 5.4 and 5.5.

9 Visual examination (9.1); ii) Measurement of diameter .of individual
iii)

iv) v) vi) vii)

wires and stranded conductor (9.2) ; Measurement of lay length (9.3) ; Measurement of weight of wires and conductor (9.4) ; Measurement of resistance of wires (9.5) * Elongation test on wires (9.6) ; and Chemical analysis (9.7).

7.3 Acceptance Tests Theacceptanw teats shall be the same as type tests. 8 SELECTION OF SAMPLES OF CONDUCTOR FOR TESTS S.1 TypeTests Three samples of wires and conductors shall be taken for each type test. The samples shall be from the wires and conductors manufactured in the presence of the inspector unless otherwise permitted by the purchaser. S.2 Acceptance Tests Samples of wires and conductors for acceptance tests shall be cut from each drum. The lay length (9.3) and resistance (9.5) shall be measured first. Then three wires from 50 mm*, and twelve wires from 105 mm2 and 160 mm* jumpers shall be taken at random and subjected to the test specified in 9.1 and 9.2. 8.2.1 criteria for Acceptance
8.2.1.1 The samples of wires and conductors taken from each drum shall be subjected to all the tests prescribed in 7.3. The wires and conductor in the drums shall be deemed to have passed the tests if the sample passes all the tests. If a .sample fails in `more, than one test, the drum shall be rejected. Should the sample fails in any one of the tests, two more samples shall be taken from the drum and subjected to all the tests. Should any sample fail in any test, the drum shall be rejected.

9.4 Measureinent of Weight of Wires and Conductor The mass of wires and stranded conductor per kilometre shall be measured by weighing three samples each of 50 cm (approximately) length by a balance having accuracy of + 1 g for conductor and + 0.1 g accuracy for wires, 9.5 Measurement of Electric
Resistance The resistance of the conductor shall be measured

at room temperature and shall be within limits specified in 4.2. 9.6 Elongation Test This test shall be performed only on wires. The load shall be applied on wires. The load shall be applied on straight lengths of wire having an original length of 250 mm. The extension shall be measured on the gauge length after the fractured ends have been fitted together provided the fracure occurs between the gauge marks and not closer t han 25 rnq to either mark. If the fracture occurs outside these limits and if the required elongation is not obtained, the test shall be discarded and another test made. 9.7 Chemical Analysis
The chemical composition shall conform to IS 191

(Part 5) : 1980.
10 PACKING AND MARKING 10.1 The conductor shall be delivered to the purchaser -properly wound on drums. A drum shall

a continuous length of conductor. The conductor shall be carefully wound on the drum, the turns being close and continuous without any overriding except on the tlrst and last turns of each layer.

4 Size of conductor, b) Length of conductor, Cl Weight of drum (net and gross);

10.2 The drums shall be of strong construction and shall generally conform to IS 1778 : 1980. The flanges of the drum shall be large enough to prevent anypossible contact between the conductor and the ground during handling or transport. No internal or external lagging is necessary but wood battens shall be nailed to the flanges, covering the whole width of the drum and the full circumference of the flanges. 10.3 Matking
10.3.1 The labelling on the drums shall include the following information :

4 Name of the manufacturer, and 0 Any other particulars specified by the
purchaser.
10.4 BIS CertificationMarkhg

The product may also be marked with Standard Mark 10.4.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
